subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core adopt FxTwitter as a supported explicit opt-in public read transport, including responsibility for its privacy disclosure, API compatibility, endpoint safety, and operational behavior?
rationale: The existing architecture can host the adapter, but source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers want a third-party public service to become a supported core dependency and configuration surface.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
options.body: Approve an explicit opt-in adapter for the proposed core read endpoints, with no automatic fallback and with privacy, capability, URL-safety, and fixture-test requirements treated as acceptance gates.

options.title: Keep authenticated transports only
options.body: Decline the core transport and retain `bird` and `xurl` as the supported live-source boundary until a different public-source policy is established.

options.title: Defer pending transport policy
options.body: Leave the request open but postpone implementation until Birdclaw defines general stability and support criteria for third-party and self-hosted read adapters.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit opt-in adapter for the proposed core read endpoints, with no automatic fallback and with privacy, capability, URL-safety, and fixture-test requirements treated as acceptance gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes Birdclaw's supported source, privacy, and configuration contract and therefore belongs to the repository's product-direction owner.
